sections.title: Group Growth & Profitability
sections.subtitle: FY2018-2022 was a deliberate cash-burn phase funding Shopee's SE Asia land-grab; FY2023 was the first profitable year. Operating and net income lines include negative values, so no Log toggle is offered on them.

sections.title: Segment Mix (Shopee / Garena / Monee)
sections.subtitle: Segment-level GMV, bookings and loan-book figures come from Sea's FY2025/Q2-2026 filings (not the group Metrics CSV, which is consolidated-only) and are shown as KPI cards and in the annotations below; the charts here use consolidated CSV data to show how segment-driven operating leverage shows up at the group level.

charts.title: Group Operating Margin: The Operating-Leverage Story
charts.annotation: Sea does not report a clean consolidated EBITDA line (D&A/lease add-backs vary by segment), so operating margin is used here. FY2025 segment adj EBITDA (a management non-GAAP measure, not this CSV): Shopee $880.6m (5.3% margin, up from just $155.8m FY2024), Garena $1,700m (56.1% margin on bookings), Monee $1,000m (26% margin).

charts.title: Capital Expenditure
charts.annotation: Shopee's logistics network (SPX Express) and Monee's technology/licensing footprint are the main capex drivers; capex intensity has stayed low relative to revenue growth, a key enabler of the FY2023+ FCF inflection.

sections.title: Cash Flow, SBC & Capital Structure
sections.subtitle: Reported free cash flow overstates distributable cash: Monee's loan-book build sits in investing activities while its pre-provision earnings sit in operating cash flow.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow
charts.annotation: Reported FCF (OCF minus capex) overstates distributable group cash: Monee's pre-provision earnings sit in operating cash flow while its ~$3.8bn FY2025 loan-book build sits in investing activities. The DCF's OpCo Owner FCF (Shopee+Garena+corporate only, component-built from segment adj EBITDA, shown as a KPI card above at $1,356.2m FY2025) excludes Monee entirely and is not a CSV column.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is Sea's consolidated revenue across Shopee (e-commerce), Garena (digital entertainment) and Monee (digital financial services).

For Sea: revenue grew from $292m (FY2015) to $22.9bn (FY2025), with H1-2026 revenue of $14.9bn (+47.4% YoY) — still accelerating even as the group matures into profitability. Shopee is 61% of revenue, Garena 18%, Monee 14%.

What to watch:

  • Shopee GMV growth guidance of ~25% for FY2026 (actual has run ahead at 28% in Q2 2026)
  • Whether TikTok Shop's ~66% 2025 GMV growth reignites a subsidy war that slows Shopee's take-rate gains

grossMargin.title: Gross Profit & Gross Margin
grossMargin.content:
Gross Margin = Gross Profit / Revenue.

For Sea: gross margin collapsed to just 1.8% in FY2018 (peak subsidy/logistics-investment era) and has recovered steadily to 44.7% in FY2025 as Shopee's logistics network matured and take rates rose. This recovery is the single clearest signal of the business's shift from land-grab to operating leverage.

profitInflection.title: The Profitability Inflection
profitInflection.content:
Operating income and net income track Sea's transition from a decade of deliberate cash-burn (funding Shopee's regional expansion) to sustained GAAP profitability.

For Sea: net income bottomed at -$2,047m in FY2021 and turned positive in FY2023 ($151m), reaching $1,578m in FY2025 — the second consecutive profitable year. H1-2026 net income to shareholders was $869m (+7.4% YoY), a much slower growth rate than revenue (+47.4%) as management trades margin for growth exactly as guided.

What to watch: whether the margin trade-off (H1-2026 operating margin 8.35% vs FY2025's 8.65%) is temporary reinvestment or a structural plateau.

marginPath.title: Margin Path
marginPath.content:
Gross, operating and net margin together show how much of Sea's gross-margin recovery has flowed through to the bottom line.

For Sea: FY2025 operating margin was 8.65%, still well below Shopee's own longer-term ad-monetization/take-rate runway (management's base case models OpCo EBITDA margin maturing to 17% by Year 10 of the DCF, versus MELI-like SE Asia e-commerce economics).

shopeeGmv.title: Shopee GMV & Gross Orders
shopeeGmv.content:
GMV (Gross Merchandise Value) is the total value of goods transacted on Shopee; gross orders is order count — together they show volume growth independent of take-rate changes.

For Sea: FY2025 Shopee GMV was $127.4bn (+26.8% YoY) across 13.9bn gross orders. Shopee holds roughly 52-59% of combined SE Asia e-commerce platform GMV, in an effective duopoly with TikTok Shop (~23-31% share and rising fast). Q2 2026 GMV growth accelerated further to 28%.

What to watch: order growth vs GMV growth (average order value trend) and any resumption of subsidy-driven order growth that doesn't convert to take-rate gains.

segmentMix.title: Segment Revenue & Adjusted EBITDA (FY2025)
segmentMix.content:
Sea reports three segments with very different economics: Shopee (e-commerce, thin but improving margins), Garena (gaming, high margin), and Monee (embedded lender, growing fast off a small base).

For Sea, FY2025: Shopee revenue $16.6bn / adj EBITDA $880.6m (5.3% margin, up from just $155.8m in FY2024 — the operating-leverage inflection). Garena revenue $2.4bn / adj EBITDA $1.7bn (a 56.1% margin on bookings — by far the highest-margin segment). Monee revenue $3.8bn / adj EBITDA $1.0bn (26% margin, growing off the smallest base).

What to watch: Shopee's EBITDA margin trajectory is the single biggest driver of group profitability given its 61% revenue share; Garena's margin durability depends on Free Fire, a single title with no announced successor.

moneeCredit.title: Monee Loan Book vs Credit-Loss Provisions
moneeCredit.content:
Monee (formerly SeaMoney) is an embedded consumer/merchant lender. Loan-book growth is not free: unlike Shopee or Garena, faster growth here means more credit risk on the balance sheet, funded by deposits payable and customer escrow (which are Monee's operating funding, not debt).

For Sea: the loan book grew from $6.83bn (FY2024) to $11.1bn (Jun-2026, +62.5% YoY). But FY2025 credit-loss provisions were $1,373m and H1-2026 provisions were $1,021m, +68.5% YoY — growing FASTER than the book. The headline 90-day NPL ratio has stayed near 1.0%, but that is weak evidence when the denominator itself is growing 62% YoY with a large unseasoned tail.

What to watch: this is the dashboard's central bear-case axis. Two years of vintage data showing provisions decelerating below book growth would be the strongest evidence against a coming credit cycle; the DCF's bear case assumes the opposite — provisions keep outpacing growth and ROA on the book compresses sharply.

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
fcf.content:
Operating Cash Flow and Reported FCF (OCF − capex) are the standard consolidated figures. Owner FCF here is a different, narrower thing: Shopee + Garena + corporate cash flow only, component-built from segment adjusted EBITDA less allocated SBC, D&A, tax, capex and working capital.

For Sea: consolidated reported FCF was $4,510.7m in FY2025 — but this overstates distributable group cash because Monee's pre-provision earnings sit in operating cash flow while its ~$3.8bn FY2025 loan-book build sits in investing activities (and its deposit funding in financing activities). The DCF therefore values Monee separately on distributable earnings (post-tax earnings less equity retained for book growth) rather than folding it into one consolidated FCF DCF, which would simultaneously overstate Monee's cash generation and fail to price its credit risk.

cashDebt.title: Cash vs Total Debt
cashDebt.content:
Sea carries a large headline cash pile against modest total debt.

For Sea: FY2025 cash was $4.16bn against total debt of $1.84bn. But headline liquidity ($3.5bn unrestricted cash + $5.6bn short-term investments at Jun-2026, ~$9.9bn combined) is not all corporate surplus: the DCF credits only $4.9bn as surplus net cash after ring-fencing ~$0.9bn against Monee deposits payable and ~$1.1bn against escrow/customer-advance backing. Deposits payable and escrow are Monee's operating funding, not debt, and are excluded from this chart's debt line.

sbcShares.title: Stock-Based Compensation & Shares Outstanding
sbcShares.content:
SBC is fully expensed as a real cost; shares outstanding shows dilution before buybacks.

For Sea: FY2025 SBC was $625.0m, about 40% of GAAP net income. Diluted shares grew from ~477m (FY2020) to ~638m (FY2025). A $1bn ADS buyback authorized Nov-2025 is running at roughly 1.3x the SBC run-rate ($431m spent through H1-2026), but the DCF holds the share count flat at 634.5m rather than assuming further net reduction.

What to watch: whether buybacks keep pace with SBC issuance as the program is exhausted through 2026.

balanceSheet.title: Shareholders' Equity vs Total Liabilities
balanceSheet.content:
Tracks balance-sheet scale as Sea moved from equity-destroying losses to compounding equity.

For Sea: equity swung negative in FY2016-2018 during peak cash-burn and has compounded since, reaching $12.5bn by FY2025 — though roughly $2.1bn of the FY2024-25 equity increase came from convertible-note conversions, not retained earnings alone. Total liabilities include Monee's deposits payable and escrow, which fund the loan book and are not treated as debt in the valuation.

capex.title: Capital Expenditure
capex.content:
CapEx is cash spent on property, equipment and technology infrastructure.

For Sea: capex has stayed modest relative to revenue (FY2025 capex $513.8m vs $22.9bn revenue, ~2.2%) even as Shopee built out its SPX Express logistics network — a capital-light model relative to physical retailers, which is part of why the FY2023+ FCF inflection was so sharp.
